sentences.text: Hello, everyone.
Welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
I'm Emily, and today we are going to a beautiful city
in Central America, Antigua, Guatemala.
Antigua is full of colors, smiles, and history.
The streets are made of stones,
the houses are painted in bright colors
and the people are warm and friendly.
When you walk in Antigua,
you feel like you were in another time.
Let's discover this magical city together.
Part two, where is Antigua?
Antigua is in the country of Guatemala.
It is in Central America, between Mexico and Honduras.
The city is surrounded by three volcanoes.
Agua, Fuego, and Acatenango.
Sometimes you can even see smoke rising from Fuego volcano.
Antigua is not a big city,
but it is very famous for its beauty and culture.
A short history of Antigua.
Antigua was founded in the 1500s by the Spanish.
It was once the capital of Guatemala.
In 1773, a big earthquake destroyed much of the city.
After that, the capital moved to Guatemala City.
But Antigua was rebuilt and protected as a historical treasure.
Today, it is part of the UNESCO World Heritage List.
Part four, the streets and buildings.
The streets of Antigua are narrow and made of stones.
You can see colorful houses, old churches,
and beautiful gardens.
Many buildings are from the Spanish colonial time.
They have red roofs and big wooden doors.
One of the most famous places is Santa Catalina Arch,
a yellow arch in the middle of the city.
It is one of the most photographed spots in Guatemala.
Part five, the people of Antigua.
People in Antigua are kind and friendly.
Many are of Mayan heritage and still wear traditional clothes.
Women wear colorful skirts and blouses
with patterns that tell their village story.
Family is very important,
and people love to celebrate together.
Many people speak Spanish,
but you can also hear local Mayan languages.
Some also speak English because of the many visitors.
Part six, food in Antigua.
Food in Antigua is delicious and full of flavor.
A popular dish is Pepian,
a thick stew made with meat, vegetables, and spices.
People also eat tamales, tostadas, and frijoles beans.
For dessert, you can try platanos fritos,
fried bananas with sugar.
And don't forget Guatemalan coffee.
It's some of the best in the world.
Many coffee farms are near Antigua and you can visit them.
Part seven, markets and crafts.
The markets in Antigua are colorful and lively.
You can buy handmade clothes, bags, jewelry, and art.
Many products are made by local women.
The colors, red, blue, yellow, green are bright and happy.
Each pattern and design has meaning and tradition.
Even if you don't buy anything,
walking in the market is a joy.
Part eight, nature around Antigua.
Antigua is surrounded by mountains and volcanoes.
You can hike up Akatonango volcano to see the sunrise.
It's an amazing view.
There are also coffee farms forests and rivers nearby.
Birds singing in the morning and the air smells fresh and sweet.
Nature makes Antigua peaceful and beautiful.
Part nine, festivals and traditions.
Antigua is famous for its festivals.
The biggest one is Samana Santa,
Holy Week before Easter.
People make carpets from flowers and colored sawdust on the streets.
Then big processions walk over them.
It's beautiful and emotional.
Other festivals celebrate independence, music, and Mayan culture.
In Antigua, every week feels like a celebration of life.
Part 10, weather in Antigua.
Antigua has a perfect climate.
It's called the land of eternal spring.
The temperature is around 20 to 25 greases all year.
Days are sunny and nights are cool.
Sometimes it rains but not for long.
People enjoy walking, drinking coffee, and relaxing outside.
Part 11, life in Antigua.
Life in Antigua is calm and joyful.
People work in shops, farms, or cafes.
Children go to school and play in the parks.
Foreign visitors come to learn Spanish or volunteer.
You can study in small schools and live with local families.
There is time to talk, rest, and enjoy the simple things.
Part 12, goodbye from Antigua.
I'm Emily, and today we explored the beautiful city of Antigua, Guatemala.
Antigua is the city of color, peace, and smiles.
It has mountains, history, and delicious food.
If you ever visit Central America, don't miss Antigua.
It will make your heart warm and happy.
Goodbye.
Or as people in Guatemala say, Adios y Gracias.
